To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the portal protein barrel of the P22 virion is a 150 Å, 12-fold symmetric, coiled-coiled, right-handed superhelical structure that is 12-fold symmetrically arranged around the portal vertex and entraps the last packaged DNA, and that the C-terminal domain of the portal interacts with closure protein to stabilize the genome during closure.

the portal barrel entraps the last 10% of the genome during genome packaging, and that the portal C terminus, the last portion of the portal to be added to the procapsid, is a key component for head-full DNA sensing and stabilization of the genome.

the bacteriophage P22 portal barrel, which is a 150 Å long coiled-coil that encases the last DNA to enter the capsid, plays a critical role in the head-full signal that triggers the final closure of the capsid and release of the genome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the portal protein of bacteriophage P22, a model for all double-stranded DNA bacteriophag
the structural basis of the portal protein in p22 bacteriophage and how the portal functions as the genome packaging and ejection valve.
the molecular mechanisms of DNA packaging and genome release, and the structural basis for these processes, in the P22 bacteriophage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the portal is the genome release valve in bacteriophages.
the structure of P22 virion is now known in its entirety.
the portal barrel is an important part of the packaging and release valve of p22.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the portal protein is the genome release valve, which controls DNA packaging and exit through a series of interactions with the terminase, scaffolding, and closure proteins and with the DNA.
this is the first structure of a virion that contains a bacteriophage genome, and it reveals the portal's role in the final stages of genome packaging.
the portal barrel acts as a valve that controls the flow of DNA into the capsid, while the C terminus acts as a plug that controls the release of DNA from the capsid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the portal is the only protein that spans the entire length of the virion and is in direct contact with the terminase, the scaffolding, the closure proteins, and the DNA.
the portal protein barrel is a dynamic valve that controls DNA packaging and release.
the portal is the only protein in the virion that is not fully buried in the capsid.
